affiliations.research_notes: A 1942 professional listing places Ornstein at Washington University; an official federal record begins his civilian OSS linguist employment in September 1942. No intervening affiliation was found.
An institutional biography describes the uncommon exact-name spouse Laszlo Ormos as a Hungarian documentary-film director in a 1937 context. It names no employer and supplies no direct OSS bridge.
The OSS board report explicitly says O'Rourke was assigned to OSS on January 15, 1944, from the Replacement Center in Cairo. It does not name a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Jacob Ornstein is confirmed as the civilian OSS linguist documented in the Congressional Record and the 1942 Washington University instructor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, doctoral title, linguist role, 1942 professional listing, and September 1942 OSS employment form a coherent identity chain.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the rare exact name across the NARA index, a 1942 professional roster, and an official federal account of OSS employment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The professional listing and official OSS start both fall in 1942.
claims.match_notes: The federal record supplies the OSS bridge; the academic source supplies the pre-OSS job.

claims.claim_text: Jacob Ornstein's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Washington University in St. Louis, where he was an instructor in Spanish and Portuguese.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Instructor in Spanish and Portuguese, Washington University, St. Louis, Missouri
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1942 professional listing places Ornstein at Washington University, and an official record begins his civilian OSS employment in September 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed identity from the rare exact name and independent official OSS record.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded in 1942 immediately before his documented September 1942 OSS employment; no intervening affiliation was found.
claims.match_notes: The sources do not literally say 'left Washington University to join OSS,' so the claim is high rather than confirmed.
